description: C++ Object-Oriented Programming Basics: Classes, Objects, Constructors, Destructors and Access Specifiers

questions.questionText: What does OOP stand for?
questions.explanation: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to define a class in C++?
questions.explanation: The class keyword is used to define a class in C++.

questions.questionText: What is an object?
questions.explanation: An object is an instance of a class and can contain the data and behavior defined by that class.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly creates an object of class Student?
questions.explanation: Student s; declares an object named s of class Student.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier makes class members accessible only within the class by default?
questions.explanation: Class members are private by default in a C++ class.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier allows members to be accessed from outside the class?
questions.explanation: Public members can be accessed from outside the class through an object, subject to the normal access rules.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier allows access within the class and its derived classes?
questions.explanation: Protected members are accessible within the class and its derived classes.

questions.questionText: What is a constructor?
questions.optionA: A special member function used to initialize objects
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special member function that is automatically called when an object is created.

questions.questionText: What is the name of a constructor?
questions.optionB: It must be the same as the class name
questions.explanation: A constructor has the same name as its class.

questions.questionText: Does a constructor have a return type?
questions.explanation: Constructors do not have a return type, not even void.

questions.questionText: When is a constructor normally called?
questions.explanation: A constructor is automatically invoked when an object is initialized or created.

questions.questionText: What is a default constructor?
questions.optionA: A constructor that takes no arguments
questions.optionB: A constructor that always takes two arguments
questions.explanation: A default constructor is a constructor that can be called with no arguments.

questions.questionText: Which constructor takes arguments to initialize an object with specific values?
questions.explanation: A parameterized constructor accepts one or more arguments for object initialization.

questions.questionText: What is a destructor?
questions.optionA: A special member function called when an object is destroyed
questions.explanation: A destructor is a special member function that is invoked when an object's lifetime ends.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is used before the class name in a destructor declaration?
questions.explanation: A destructor is declared using the tilde (~) followed by the class name.

questions.questionText: Can a class have more than one constructor?
questions.explanation: A class can have multiple constructors with different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: What is constructor overloading?
questions.optionA: Using multiple constructors with different parameter lists
questions.optionC: Using a constructor as a destructor
questions.explanation: Constructor overloading means defining multiple constructors with different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: Which operator is commonly used to access members of an object?
questions.explanation: The dot operator (.) is used to access members through an object.

questions.questionText: Which operator is commonly used to access members through a pointer to an object?
questions.explanation: The arrow operator (->) is used to access members through a pointer to an object.

questions.questionText: What is encapsulation?
questions.optionA: Bundling data and methods together and controlling access to them
questions.explanation: Encapsulation combines data and related methods in a class and allows access to be controlled.

questions.questionText: Which OOP concept hides internal implementation details and exposes only necessary functionality?
questions.explanation: Abstraction focuses on exposing essential features while hiding unnecessary implementation details.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class Test { public: Test() { cout << "A"; } }; int main() { Test t; }
questions.explanation: Creating object t automatically calls the constructor, which prints A.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class Test { public: ~Test() { cout << "D"; } }; int main() { Test t; }
questions.explanation: When t goes out of scope at the end of main, its destructor is called and prints D.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier is the default for members of a C++ class?
questions.explanation: Members of a C++ class are private by default.

questions.questionText: Which access specifier is the default for members of a C++ struct?
questions.explanation: Members of a C++ struct are public by default, unlike members of a class.
